memory_update.text: MKSI should be tracked as the strongest US-listed underfollowed proxy for advanced packaging wet chemistry, plating, package-substrate surface treatment, and copper/RDL process exposure through Atotech.
FORM should be tracked as an HBM and advanced-package yield-control candidate through probe cards and known-good-die testing, not as a substrate maker.

ONTO should be tracked as an inspection/metrology beneficiary of AI-package complexity, especially where panel substrates, 3D bump metrology, RDL, and macro defect inspection become yield bottlenecks.

US-listed direct pure-play exposure to FC-BGA substrates, ABF insulating film, and copper adhesion chemistry appears limited; many core substrate and materials names are Japan/Taiwan-listed, so US-listed exposure is mostly adjacent through chemistry, test, inspection, and OSAT capacity.

Layer 2 should verify whether any US-listed ADRs or OTC securities for Japan/Taiwan substrate and chemistry leaders are investable enough for inclusion, while keeping this Layer 1B list focused on primary US exchange-listed names.

node: HBM and AI accelerator advanced-package substrates, insulating films, and surface chemistry
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a US-listed second-order universe around advanced packaging rather than the primary GPU/HBM winners. The cleanest underfollowed mapping is not pure FC-BGA substrate manufacturing, where many key players are Japan/Taiwan-listed, but adjacent US-listed suppliers to the same chokepoint: advanced packaging chemistry and plating, package inspection/metrology, HBM wafer/package test, and outsourced advanced packaging capacity. MKS/Atotech, Onto Innovation, FormFactor, and Amkor are plausible US-listed candidates to track, with MKS/Atotech and FormFactor closest to obscure chokepoint economics. All are research candidates only, not recommendations.
